versions.name: 1.0.0 - Trust & Stability
versions.summary: Fix paywall confusion, billing trust, and ad abuse that are causing churn and 1-star reviews.
versions.rationale: Findings 1-3 carry the highest severity and user impact. They directly cause users to abandon the app or label it a scam. Stabilizing these trust surfaces is a prerequisite for any longer-term value work.

versions.name: 1.1.0 - Core Experience
versions.summary: Make personalization honor user constraints and improve workout content quality.
versions.rationale: Once trust is restored, the most polarizing feature — the workout library — becomes the focus. Finding 4 and finding 5 show users either love the short/varied workouts or hate repetitions, AI-slop, and ignored safety settings. These are medium-frequency but high-impact issues for retention and safety.

versions.name: 1.2.0 - Inclusive Wellness
versions.summary: Rebrand onboarding and imagery to be inclusive and wellness-first.
versions.rationale: Finding 6 is a small but vocal signal that the app's weight-loss-first framing and AI body imagery alienate wellness-focused users. The change is low-cost and aligns the brand with a broader, more inclusive fitness audience.

planningFactors.rationale: 16.8% of reviews describe paywall regression that turns long-time users into detractors. The same evidence also shows a subset of subscribers who love the app, so the fix is not to remove the subscription but to make the free tier and premium boundary honest and valuable.

Billing failures directly break the subscription value proposition and brand trust. 7.8% of reviews report immediate charges, cancellation failures, or account lockouts, often using the word 'scam'. Fixing this is essential before any monetization expansion.

10.4% of reviews cite 90-second or unclosable ads and Shein redirects as churn triggers. Some users explicitly accept ads as a fair trade for free access, so the goal is to keep the ad-supported tier but make it non-abusive and functional.

Personalization failures are safety-relevant (especially prenatal) and directly contradict the app's customization promise. Frequency is low (2.4%) but the damage to affected users is severe and the feature differentiates the app from competitors.

The workout library is the most polarizing feature: 14.8% of reviews are split between 5-star praise for short, effective, varied sessions and strong criticism of repetitive or AI-generated content. Improving freshness while keeping the short format serves the largest audience.

A small but vocal segment (1.2% of reviews) finds the weight-loss-first framing and AI body imagery actively harmful. The change is low-cost and improves brand inclusivity and alignment with wellness values.
